key_insight: The paper turns tree-adjoining grammars into a Bayesian equation-discovery framework that infers both model structure and parameters with uncertainty quantification.
engineering_relevance: This enables physics-informed system identification that can discover interpretable dynamical models while supporting grey-box modeling for real engineering data.
method: Define a generative prior over TAG tree structures and their parameters.
Use Reversible-Jump MCMC with structure-preserving tree moves to sample the joint posterior.
Handle one-step-ahead prediction with conjugate proposals and simulation-based training with likelihood-free inference.
evidence_signal: The approach was validated on a simulated polynomial NARX system, the Silverbox benchmark, and Christchurch Bay Tower wave-loading data, where a Morison’s-equation-based grey-box model outperformed the physics-driven baseline.
watch_item: Reversible-Jump MCMC and likelihood-free inference can be computationally demanding and may require careful proposal design and tuning.
paper_title: Equation discovery with Bayesian tree-adjoining grammars
